candidates.tagline: $10 lollipop. One use. Three songs. Disposable circuit board included.
candidates.story: Lollipop Star launched at CES 2026 as a single-use bone-conduction candy: bite the stick, hear music through your jaw, then throw away the lollipop AND the embedded electronics — a micro motor, capacitor, and memory chip — every single time.
candidates.why_funny: The entire premise of sustainable electronics is violated by a product whose core design is 'discard the circuit board after 30 seconds of Akon.'
candidates.alt: The Lollipop Star product showing a translucent blue lollipop with a large electronic vibration module capsule at the base of the stick, alongside branded packaging reading 'Pop It, Play It' and 'Taste the Music — Akon'.

candidates.tagline: $2.2 billion stadium — view sold separately, not included
candidates.story: The Buffalo Bills opened brand-new Highmark Stadium in August 2026 to viral complaints: fans who paid tens of thousands for Personal Seat Licenses found their $2.2B views blocked by concrete ledges, glass safety barriers, and staircase railings — and the architect called it 'intentional design'.
candidates.why_funny: A stadium costing $2.2 billion managed to block paying fans' sightlines with concrete and glass, then the designer said the obstructions were a feature, not a bug.
candidates.alt: Buffalo Bills fans peering over a thick concrete platform labelled 'BRUCE SMITH 78' at the new Highmark Stadium, looking through a glass safety barrier in an attempt to see the field below.
